messages:
alex: heads-up — I ran a short profiling pass comparing adaptive micro-batching + kernel selector vs static batching for Llama-7B, Mixtral-7B and Qwen-7B. posting highlights and raw snippets below.
maria: nice, curious about p99 impact at larger ctx lengths. did you include RoPE scaling variants?
alex: yes — tested three RoPE configs: vanilla, fractional-scale 0.9, and fractional-scale 0.7. also toggled `fused-attn-v2` vs `split-kernel` paths.
tj: quick summary pls (tl;dr numbers) so I can update the runtime heuristics doc.
alex: tl;dr: adaptive micro-batching + head-aware kernel choice wins for throughput and keeps p99 within SLO for mixed traffic. numbers (tokens/s) at ctx=512, batch cap=16: Llama-7B: static 3.8k, adaptive 5.1k; Mixtral-7B: static 2.6k, adaptive 3.9k; Qwen-7B: static 2.9k, adaptive 4.2k.
maria: p99s?
alex: p99 at same point: Llama static 72ms -> adaptive 52ms; Mixtral static 96ms -> adaptive 68ms; Qwen static 81ms -> adaptive 59ms.
lee: impressive. did you isolate KV cache eviction artifacts? last time we saw p99 spikes when many short-context requests came in and small KV caches were thrashing.
alex: good call. I instrumented KV hits/misses. perf-bot posted the KV summary:
perf-bot: KV SUMMARY (snippet)
```
model    kv_hit_rate batch_eff ctx_tail_tokens
llama7b  0.74        0.63      0.12
mixtral7b0.61        0.58      0.22
qwen7b   0.68        0.66      0.10
```
alex: adaptive approach boosted kv_hit_rate by prefetching common prefixes and grouping by context-length bucket before batching. that lowered effective tail token churn.
samir: curious about kernel selector rules — how are we mapping head/kv dims to fused vs split?
alex: rule we tested: if model heads <= 32 and kv_dim_per_head <= 64, prefer `fused-attn-v2` up to ctx 2048. else prefer `split-kernel` or `block-attn` for ctx>4096. we also added a fallback: if observed batch shape has >50% short requests (<128) and >10% long (>2048), we split pipeline (shorts -> low-latency path, longs -> throughput path).
tj: did you measure kernel switch overhead? switching kernels mid-batch can be expensive.
alex: yes — kernel switch penalty ~0.9ms on A100 if cached kernels present, ~3.8ms cold. so we only switch at batch boundaries and avoid mixing kernels inside a batch. adaptive scheduler groups by kernel preference with a 15ms max queue-delay budget.
maria: RoPE results? tradeoffs?
alex: fractional RoPE 0.9 gave the best throughput on Mixtral with negligible quality regression in our eval set. fractional 0.7 improved throughput another ~8% but increased hallucination rate on instruction eval by ~1.2% for Llama variants. Qwen tolerated 0.7 better.
lee: are these RoPE settings exposed per-model or per-deployment?
alex: per-model config right now (we added entries in model-catalog): `rope_scale: 1.0|0.9|0.7` and `kernel_hint: fused|split|auto`. default remains `auto`.
perf-bot: PROFILE: Mixtral-7B ctx=8192, batch=2 -> tokens/s 890, p99 420ms, kv_hit_rate 0.47
maria: 8192 is rough. for those contexts, what batching strategy? continuous batching or immediate passthrough?
alex: immediate passthrough for >4096 unless we hit a sustained queue; we observed that batching longs hurts latency and has minimal throughput benefits for these models due to memory/attention kernel behavior.
samir: any kernel-level anomalies? e.g., reduction in occupancy for certain head dims?
alex: yes — Mixtral weirdness: head_count 64 with kv_per_head 128 caused the fused kernel to under-utilize warp units when ctx < 256. hence the head-aware rule. we also saw a regression after a recent cuBLAS bump where GEMM tiling changed — manifested as 7-12% throughput drop for certain shapes. opened infra-issue #674.
lee: action item: add a diagnostic metric for kernel-occupancy and GEMM-shape hit-rate to runtime traces.
alex: already added a lightweight counter and flame sample. logs show GEMM-shape histogram: `[(64x128), (32x128), (64x64)]` with the middle bin spiking post-PR.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: adaptive-batcher v2 to staging at 2026-04-02T18:22Z (canary 5%).
maria: plan for rollout? metrics to watch?
alex: watch tokens/s, p99, kv_hit_rate, and kernel-switch-count. set alert if p99 increases >15% or kv_hit_rate drops >10% vs baseline. also watch GEMM-shape histogram for the flagged bins.
samir: test matrix suggestion: run the adaptive strategy across model-catalog combinations: Llama-7B/13B, Mixtral-7B, Mixtral-8x16, Qwen-7B/14B at ctx buckets [128,512,2048,8192] and batch_caps [1,4,8,16]. collect tokens/s + p50/p95/p99 + kv_hit_rate + kernel_pref_ratio.
alex: agreed — I have a script. ran a smoke matrix and attached the headlined csv to the staging run (link: https://redwood-internal/perf/1802345678).
maria: any immediate config recs we can ship to prod?
alex: conservative recs: default `kernel_hint=auto`, but set `rope_scale=0.9` for Mixtral-7B in Dedicated and Private profiles; set batch_cap=8 for Qwen-7B on A100 to avoid p99 knee; enable adaptive-batcher-v2 with queue budget 15ms.
lee: pushed a PR updating runtime heuristics doc and model-catalog. tagging @oncall to monitor canary.
alex: notes for follow-up: 1) quantify quality delta for rope 0.9 across our eval suites, 2) run long-tail test with synthetic short+long interleaving to stress KV eviction, 3) validate GEMM regression fix from infra team.
maria: thanks alex — this is great. can you paste the small config diff we should apply in prod?
alex: config diff snippet:
```
models:
  mixtral-7b:
    rope_scale: 0.9
    kernel_hint: auto
    batch_cap: 8
  qwen-7b:
    rope_scale: 1.0
    kernel_hint: auto
    batch_cap: 8
runtime:
  adaptive_batcher:
    enabled: true
    queue_budget_ms: 15
```
maria: perfect. i'll checkpoint and schedule the canary monitor. :thumbsup:
alex: thanks — will follow up with full CSV and flame traces in the staging run.
